name: Toast Inc

events.what: Chief Accounting Officer appointed (not a CEO or CFO change)
CFO Elena Gomez also named President (role expansion, same person; outside the 18-month window)

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Toast's margin is adjusted EBITDA as a percent of RECURRING GROSS PROFIT (subscription plus fintech gross profit), not of revenue. The 40%+ long-term target has no year ('timing firmly in our control'). The earlier dated target was 30% to 35% medium-term (2 to 3 years from Feb 2023), reached in 2025 (34%). Street margins in consensus_ebitda_margin_by_fy are EBITDA / revenue (11.0%, 11.9%, 13.1%) and are not comparable; the gap math uses consensus EBITDA over VA consensus recurring gross profit (data_company_data, fetched 2026-09-28). No dated rate: 2026 is framed as 'modest margin expansion'.

statements.quote: Finally, we are confident in our path to adjusted EBITDA margins of 40% or more.
statements.speaker: Elena Gomez

statements.quote: When you think about the growth equation, we've talked about, you know, 20% recurring gross profit. We think of that as a floor for the next few years, while at the same time driving 30%-35% adjusted EBITDA margins, and so we have ambition over the long term to drive that adjusted EBITDA to 40%. That's over the long term.
statements.speaker: Elena Gomez

statements.quote: That said, our margin framework is to hit that head on remains unchanged, right? We're targeting 40% margins over the long term. And that pace, this is really important. The pace at which we drive that margin is in our control.
statements.speaker: Elena Gomez
statements.doc_title: Toast Inc Q4 FY2025 Earnings Call

statements.quote: We plan to continue operating with this general framework focused on sustained growth and gradual margin expansion as long as our investments are meeting our expectations. That keeps us on a path to 40%+ long-term adjusted EBITDA margins with the timing firmly in our control.
statements.speaker: Elena Gomez

street.gap_assumption: No target year, so FY2028 is used as the first year consensus reaches the target. Recurring gross profit basis on both sides: consensus EBITDA / VA consensus recurring gross profit = 35.6% FY2026, 37.7% FY2027, 40.9% FY2028, 44.1% FY2029. The street is 92 bps ABOVE 40% in FY2028. Revenue-basis figures are shown in consensus_ebitda_margin_by_fy only for reference.
street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (Visible Alpha) plus data_company_data recurring gross profit

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q1 2026, Q2 2026], adj. EBITDA over VA recurring gross profit (Q1 $179M/$520M vs $133M/$394M; Q2 $221M/$585M vs $161M/$447M). Management stated Q2 margin 'expanded 240 basis points to 37%', helped by about a $10M tariff refund (Gomez, doc 121323); the computed figure differs because it uses VA rounded recurring gross profit. FY2026 adj. EBITDA guide raised to $805M to $825M, by less than the Q2 beat because upside is reinvested.

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus: the 40%+ adjusted EBITDA / recurring gross profit target has no year, and consensus reaches 40.9% in FY2028 and 44.1% in FY2029. Also there is no CEO, CFO, deal or activist event in the window (only CAO, CRO and one director), and 12-month forward EBITDA revisions are -1.0%.
verdict: Not a GXO setup: down 41% but only at the 31st percentile of its EV/EBITDA range, with no CEO, CFO or deal catalyst, and the CFO's undated 40%+ (of recurring gross profit) target is already exceeded by FY2028 consensus (40.9%). Management is choosing to reinvest rather than expand margin faster.
open_questions: Does the street's 40.9% FY2028 margin assume less reinvestment than management's 'gradual margin expansion' framework, so the risk is a cut rather than upside?
Will Toast attach a year to 40%+ or raise the long-term target given the core already runs above 40%?
Who replaces CRO Jonathan Vassil (leaving 2026-12-31), and does go-to-market spend change?
